title: Fetchlinks collection run (contract v3)
description: What one collection attempt did. Exactly one of these rides in every batch that reaches the spool, including a run that collected nothing and a run in which every source failed -- those are precisely the runs an operator needs to see. It carries counts, categories and one short message per failure; complete logs and tracebacks stay on the collector's own machine.

elapsed_ms.description: Measured with a monotonic clock rather than subtracting the two timestamps, which an NTP correction can make nonsensical.

result.description: ok when every enabled source succeeded, partial when some did and some did not, failed when none did. Zero posts is not a failure: a quiet hour is a valid successful result.

posts_collected.description: Posts handed to this batch. Not posts stored -- deduplication is the publisher's decision and belongs to its own record.

sources.description: One entry per source the run considered, including ones it skipped because they are switched off.

subtasks.description: Work done alongside collection that can fail on its own, such as refreshing a follows snapshot. Kept separate so a failed follows sync does not read as a failed collection.

errorKind.description: A small stable vocabulary, so counts can be compared across weeks. Empty when nothing failed. Deliberately not an exception class name: those change when a library is upgraded.

errorMessage.description: One short, truncated message for the operator. Bounded because this is the one field carrying text from a stranger's website.

channels_attempted.description: Feeds, subreddits or accounts this source tried. One for sources that are a single stream.

items_returned.description: Items the provider handed over before filtering, so a source that is being served nothing looks different from one whose items are all being discarded.

errors.description: How many channels failed for each reason. An object rather than a list so a reader cannot see the same category twice.

scope.description: Which slice the subtask covered, for work that runs once per instance. Empty when there is only one.
